artifacts.notes: The institute identifies the source as CSKC-INP, Coretta Scott King Collection, In Private Hands, sermon file, folder 59.
artifacts.rights_basis: The King Institute states that it cannot grant permission to reproduce King's writings and directs permissions to the King Estate's licensor. No transcript, manuscript image, screenshot, or page byte is retained; consumers may paraphrase the protected sermon and quote only independently public-domain biblical wording.

edition.notes: The institute gives 25 September 1955 and Montgomery with question marks. Its paragraph 139 reports King's file-folder note, 'Preached at Dexter, Sept (4th Sun), 1955.' Preserve this uncertainty rather than converting it to a certain date or place.
edition.publication: Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute archival transcript, consulted 2026-07-28
edition.title: Pride Versus Humility: The Parable of the Pharisee and the Publican, Sermon at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church

passages.context: Paragraphs 111-118 turn the Pharisee's ceremonialism into an indictment of imperial oppression, lynching, the acquittal in the Emmett Till murder case, and Christians who separate emotional worship from moral life; paragraph 118 returns to disparaging comparison. Paragraphs 136-137 return to the publican's distance, shame, and plea for mercy. Paragraph 139 preserves the file-folder dating note. This supports a civil-rights redirection of the parable, not quotation of King's protected wording or certainty about date and place.
passages.notes: Protected sermon: paraphrase only. The ancient biblical plea may be quoted from the publication's registered public-domain Bible witness, not copied as King's protected expression.

work.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
work.description: King's handwritten Dexter Avenue sermon manuscript on Luke 18:9-14, using the parable to oppose ceremonial piety detached from moral life, condemnation of others, and spiritual pride.
